title: Gospel of Thomas, sayings 51-57 (Nag Hammadi Codex II, pages 42-43)
source: Nag Hammadi Codex II page photographs (Claremont Colleges Digital Library, Nag Hammadi Archive) + Coptic SCRIPTORIUM edition by Paul Dilley (CC BY 4.0) + English by Mark M. Mattison (public domain)
description: Gospel of Thomas, sayings 51-57, in the Coptic of Nag Hammadi Codex II, pages 42-43, with each saying linked to the photograph of the papyrus page and an English translation.
introduction:
The Gospel of Thomas is a collection of 114 sayings attributed to Jesus, introduced as the hidden sayings written down by Didymos Judas Thomas. The only complete copy is the second tractate of Nag Hammadi Codex II, a papyrus book in Coptic copied in the 4th century and found near Nag Hammadi in Upper Egypt in 1945; it is now in the Coptic Museum, Cairo (inv. 10544). Greek fragments of the work survive in three Oxyrhynchus papyri (P. Oxy. 1, 654 and 655), which are not shown here.

This entry covers the sayings 51-57, which begin on codex page 42; the end of saying 57 is on page 43. The Coptic is given line by line; the small numbers are codex page and line (for example 33.5), so each line can be found on the photograph. Page and line breaks follow the Coptic SCRIPTORIUM edition by Paul Dilley, which he made from the photographs of The Facsimile Edition of the Nag Hammadi Codices, the negatives shown here.

Photograph: Codex II page 42, A-Series negative by Basile Psiroukis, Facsimile Edition p. 52, CCDL nha 2871; Nag Hammadi Archive of the Institute for Antiquity and Christianity, Claremont Colleges Digital Library. Checked on the photograph: page 42 line 1 begins 'ⲁⲩⲱ ⲁϥⲟⲩⲱⲛϩ ⲉ[ⲃ]ⲟⲗ ϩⲛ̄ⲧⲟⲩϩⲓⲕⲱⲛ ⲉⲩ' and line 35 reads 'ⲉ̣ⲛ̣[ⲁⲛⲟ]ⲩϥ⳿ ⲁⲡⲉϥϫⲁϫⲉ ⲉⲓ ⲛ̄ⲧⲟⲩϣⲏ⳿' (the top line is damaged at the left; the last line begins after a break).
translator_notes: Coptic: Coptic SCRIPTORIUM edition (Paul C. Dilley), version 6.2.0, CC BY 4.0, shown in the manuscript's own spelling with words grouped as bound groups. Editorial signs are the edition's: square brackets mark letters lost in a gap (restored by the editor, or dots for the number of lost letters), a dot under a letter marks an uncertain reading, round brackets write out a letter abbreviated by a stroke at a line end, angle brackets mark letters added by the editor, curly brackets letters the editor removes, double square brackets letters erased by the scribe.

The small numbers in the Coptic are codex page and line (page.line) as marked in the edition. Where a word is divided between two lines on the papyrus, the edition sometimes keeps the word whole on one line, so a line can begin a few letters earlier or later on the photograph (for example 39.33-34, and the page change inside saying 13).

English: Mark M. Mattison, The Gospel of Thomas (public domain). Mattison's symbols: [ ] gap in the text, ( ) editorial insertion, / \ editorial correction of a scribal error. The saying headings are his.

translation.text:
His disciples said to him, "When will the dead have rest, and when will the new world come?"

He said to them, "What you're looking for has already come, but you don't know it."

His disciples said to him, "Twenty-four prophets have spoken in Israel, and they all spoke of you."

He said to them, "You've ignored the Living One right in front of you, and you've talked about those who are dead."

translation.text:
His disciples said to him, "Is circumcision useful, or not?"

He said to them, "If it were useful, parents would have children who are born circumcised. But the true circumcision in spirit has become profitable in every way."

43.6ⲟⲩ ⲅⲁⲣ ⲙ̄ⲡⲱϩ︤ⲥ︥ ⲛ̄ⲍⲓⲍⲁⲛⲓⲟⲛ ⲛⲁⲟⲩⲱⲛϩ
43.7ⲉⲃⲟⲗ⳿ ⲥⲉϩⲟⲗⲟⲩ ⲛ̄ⲥⲉⲣⲟⲕϩⲟⲩ
translation.text: Jesus said, "My Fathers' kingdom can be compared to someone who had [good] seed. Their enemy came by night and sowed weeds among the good seed. The person didn't let anyone pull out the weeds, 'so that you don't pull out the wheat along with the weeds,' they said to them. 'On the day of the harvest, the weeds will be obvious. Then they'll be pulled out and burned.'"
translation.scan_note: On page 42 lines 32-35; page 43 lines 1-7 (Codex II page 42, A-Series negative by Basile Psiroukis, Facsimile Edition p. 52, CCDL nha 2871; Codex II page 43, A-Series negative by Basile Psiroukis, Facsimile Edition p. 53, CCDL nha 2914). Opens 'ⲡⲉ' at 42.32; ends 'ⲉⲃⲟⲗ⳿ ⲥⲉϩⲟⲗⲟⲩ ⲛ̄ⲥⲉⲣⲟⲕϩⲟⲩ' at 43.7.
